name: Boyd Varty
role: Lion tracker; author, The Lion Tracker's Guide to Life
take: Attention is the discipline of the tracker. The information is there — you have to teach yourself to see it.
kept: I don't know where we are going, but I know exactly how to get there.
Let the natural world be your teacher.
Things that looked like the end of people so often turn out to be the catalyst of their growth.
A great danger is the danger of no danger.

name: Joe Hudson
take: Self-understanding beats self-improvement. What you're ashamed of, you keep doing — so stop hiding it.
kept: Anything you can get defensive about is true.
Unspoken expectations are premeditated resentments.
If you can't say no easily, you can't be trusted.
You guarantee failure privately by not exposing yourself to failure publicly.

name: David Sutcliffe
take: External validation won't fill an internal void. The satisfaction is in the climb, not the summit.
kept: Extreme ownership: the buck stops here.
Take risks, take action — if it isn't working, try a different approach.
Just a walk can solve most of your problems.
We are not meant to be happy so much as to try — the satisfaction is in the climb.

name: Adam Lane Smith
take: You're built for challenge, not complication. Streamline the life — and you aren't meant to do it solo.
kept: You are built for challenge, not complication — simplify the life.
There is no such thing as overworked, only under-rested.
When you're stuck, go to people who can show the way. Nobody is meant to operate solo.

name: James Sexton
role: Trial lawyer; on relationships & human nature
take: People want to know the rules. The real work is saying the thing you're not saying out loud.

name: Michael Easter
role: Author, The Comfort Crisis & Scarcity Brain
take: Almost everything that makes you better is hard. Choose to be slightly uncomfortable, on purpose.
kept: The vast majority of things that are good for us are hard.
We can spend our dopamine or invest it.
Boredom is a signal that the return on investment is running thin.
If you want to do things other people don't do, you have to do things other people aren't doing.

name: Richard Thaler
take: Make what you want less of harder, and what you want more of easier. Design your own defaults.
kept: Make it hard to do what you want less of, and easy to do what you want more of.
People save when a structure saves for them — design the default.
What is obvious to me that is not obvious to others?
The more bidders there are, the less you should bid.

name: Andy Galpin
take: Adaptation is a byproduct of stress. If you want to change, you have to impose the demand.
kept: Adaptation happens as a byproduct of stress — impose the demand.
The primary driver of strength is intensity; of muscle, volume.
Soreness is not the measure of a good workout.

name: Sahil Bloom
take: Time is the asset of incalculable value. The billionaire would trade it all to be where you are now.
kept: Time is life's toothpaste: you squeeze hardest when there's least left.
People are like bikes — stationary they're hard to steer, moving they're easy.
You cannot answer the big questions of life standing still.
Friends come as leaves, branches, and roots. Know which is which.

name: Scott Galloway
take: Every great yes comes after a lot of no's. Control what you can and take as many shots as you can.
kept: Focus on the things you can control, and take as many shots as you can.
People are flawed — put away the scorecard and work from there.
What if the way you are going is actually okay?

name: Jason Calacanis
role: Angel investor; This Week in Startups
take: The system is so easy to win — why cheat? Have cool friends and build cool things.
kept: Once you're lucky, twice you're good.
Find your format, then iterate relentlessly.
When I challenge you I'm not disagreeing — I'm helping you sharpen the position.
Construct your life around what pulls you out of bed.

name: Tommy Mello
take: Do more than others — if it's easy, everyone's doing it. Share a future with people, not a past.
kept: Revenue is for vanity, profit is for sanity.
Just go for no — don't fear rejection.
Negotiate for things you don't think are possible.
Don't set a yearly goal; set weekly and monthly ones.

name: Josh Stech
take: Equity is selling pieces of yourself — the most valuable thing you own. Learn to sell. It's when, not if.
kept: Tough decisions, easy life; easy decisions, tough life — Jerzy Gregorek's line.
Early metrics can't be results; measure activity.
You are the average of the five people you spend the most time with, so pick people who leave you no option but to rise.

name: Maor Shlomo
take: Build something you actually use. Building in public and giving credit worked extremely well.
kept: Build something you actually use.
Ask daily: what do I need to work on, and what do I want to work on?
Don't be afraid of feedback.

name: Mike Jones
take: The strength of a founder is building with people smarter than you. Purpose is not optional.
kept: Mercenary versus missionary founder — know which one you are.
Be good at asking for help.
It's not what I did previously; it's what am I going to do.

name: John Morgan
take: If work feels like play, it gets easier. Hunt with your hobbies. Sell the sizzle, not the steak.
kept: Failure can be your friend — do things you're interested in.
When work isn't work, you're a lot better at it. Hunt with your hobbies.
Bullets before bombs.

name: Furqan Rydhan
take: Impatient with action, patient with results. Take the risks with the biggest leverage — survive first.
kept: Impatient with action, patient with results.
For emerging tech there is only one rule: survive.
Think, decide, act — and shrink the delay before act.

name: Daniel Broukhim
take: Pivoted an agency into a membership platform without ego. Build the muscle, then the machine.

name: Reid Hoffman
take: To build something big you do things that don't scale — right up until the day you have to scale them.

name: William Hockey
take: Good founders bet on themselves and take extreme risk. Find the boring thing you'll stay curious about for a decade.
kept: Good founders bet on themselves and take extreme risk.
Venture money is like heroin — don't optimise the company for raising.
Find the most boring thing you can stay interested in for decades.
Resilience and persistence.

name: Chris Camillo
take: Don't cut your flowers to water your weeds. Compete only where you have an unfair, specific edge.
kept: Don't cut your flowers to water your weeds.
Compete only where you have a specific, unfair advantage.
The riskiest thing you can do is spend this year standing where you stood last year.

name: Mark Bertolini
role: Former CEO, Aetna; co-CEO, Oscar Health
take: Courage is moving without perfect information. Never waste a good crisis — there's opportunity in everything.
kept: I thought I was right all the time; really I was right about a third of it. The point is deciding and moving.
Nothing should stay the same unless it stands on its own — challenge everything.
Never count anyone else's money.
Never waste a good crisis.

name: Chris Josephs
take: Turned a transparency project into a product. Sunlight as strategy — memes made a dry issue land.
kept: Sunlight as strategy: turn a transparency project into distribution.
Memes made a dry issue land with an audience that reads nothing else.

name: Damon West
take: Be the coffee bean — change the water you're in. Habits are the promises you keep to yourself.
kept: Be the coffee bean — change the pot you're in.
You don't have to win every fight, but you have to fight every fight.
Find a way to do your time; don't let your time do you.
Integrity is what you do when no one is watching.

name: Michael Chernow
take: On the other side of fear is freedom — so look for the fear. The one job in life: get back up.
kept: The hard way is the right way.
Anybody can change, anytime. Period.
Don't leave before the miracle happens.
On the other side of fear is freedom — look for the fear.

name: Matt Boda
take: You're never alone and you're going to be okay. Being helpful to others is how you help yourself.
kept: Being helpful to others is how you help yourself.
The only thing bigger than a drink or a drug was a dream.
Beyond all the connections — what can you, yourself, provide?

name: Teddy Tarantino
take: Better to be clean dreaming about using than using dreaming about being clean. Follow your word.
kept: Do the hard thing; do the right thing.
Every single relationship has boundaries.
Long-term thinking: do things for the long term, and follow your word.

name: Jeremy London
take: Dealing with fear is temporary; dealing with regret is permanent. Once you start, consistency compounds.
kept: Dealing with fear is temporary; dealing with regret is permanent.
Be good every day rather than great every so often.
Only doing the work gets the work done.
Health is wealth — you can't buy back time.

name: Brandon Novak
take: From total wreckage back to purpose. The point was never the fall — it's the daily decision to rebuild.

name: Fred Again
take: Do the unconventional thing that works for you. You won't make the best thing every time — but make something.
kept: Do the unconventional thing that works for you.
You won't make the best thing every time — but make something.
Becoming an expert, and seeing someone as an expert, is beautiful.

name: Sebastian Stan
take: Step out and feel it — face the music. Life is lived in the gray; it can be both.
kept: Step out and feel it — face the music.
Life is lived in the gray; it can be both.
Rejection is healthy: coming back up.

name: Cynthia Boccara
role: Chiropractor; Major League Pickleball medical team — 'the Pickleball Doc'
take: The joint that hurts is rarely the joint that failed. Look upstream and downstream before you treat the knee.
kept: Play until we're ninety, safely.
It is the innate intelligence in the body that does the healing — not me, not the tape, not the scraper.
The so-called knee problem in this sport is usually a lateral hamstring, and it starts with a glute that sits all day.
Warm up dynamically to turn on the line between brain and feet; people fall because that line was quiet.

name: Ben Yahalom
role: CEO, True Classic — bootstrapped to nine figures; first outside capital in 2025 at an $850M valuation
take: Every dollar either generates revenue or visibly supports it. If a request can't say which, it doesn't pass.
kept: Before you hire: can we articulate the need, can AI do it, can we outsource it. The hire is the last resort.
Chefs reason from first principles; cooks follow recipes. Too many cooks in every kitchen is a hiring problem.
Performance branding — the ad converts and leaves a mark. Measure both, even though only one is on the P&L.

name: Pablos Holman
take: Things are more malleable than you think. Find the assumption you are carrying that may not be true.
kept: My whole career I have only worked on things that are cool or interesting, and I will optimise that over everything else.
Go further with your boredom — the boring basics are where the needle moves.
What is the worst thing that can happen? Answer it honestly and most fear evaporates.
Do what you are good at and hire for what you are bad at.
